question: What is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Citric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Citric acid** is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges, lemons, limes, and grapefruits.
 
• It gives these fruits their characteristic tangy and sour flavor.
 
• Citric acid is a weak organic acid with the chemical formula **C₆H₈O₇**.
 
• This acid plays a crucial role in the **citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle)**, a key metabolic pathway in living organisms.
 
• It is widely used in the food and beverage industry as a natural preservative and flavor enhancer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactic acid:** Found in sour milk products like yogurt and responsible for muscle fatigue during intense physical activity.
 
• **Tartaric acid:** Found naturally in grapes and bananas; used in baking powder as a leavening agent.
 
• **Acetic acid:** The primary component of vinegar, giving it its distinctive sharp odor and taste.
 
• Citrus fruits are an excellent source of vitamin C (**ascorbic acid**), which supports immune health and acts as an antioxidant.
 
• Citric acid has applications beyond food, including in cleaning products, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics due to its chelating and pH-regulating properties.
